summary: Generate all well-formed strings with n pairs of parentheses.
mainInsight: Build the string left to right, adding '(' while fewer than n are used and ')' while it would not exceed the number of '(' so far; every string built this way is valid, so nothing needs to be filtered afterwards.

approaches.name: Brute force + filter
approaches.summary: Generate all 2^(2n) strings and keep the valid ones.

approaches.name: Backtracking with open/close counts
approaches.summary: Add '(' if opens < n; add ')' if closes < opens.

approaches.name: Dynamic programming / closure numbers
approaches.summary: Build n from smaller solutions: ( A ) B.

personalSolution.approach: Backtracking that prunes invalid prefixes after the fact
personalSolution.notes: Correct. Add a return at the base case and prune before recursing.

promptVariants: What rules define a valid prefix of parentheses?
Which two conditions allow adding a character?
options: '(' allowed while opens < n; ')' allowed while closes < opens
Any character may be placed at any time, filter at the end
Only alternating '(' and ')' characters, one after the other
')' first and then '(' until both counts hit n, one by one
cards.answer: '(' allowed while opens < n; ')' allowed while closes < opens
cards.explanation: These constraints ensure every prefix can be extended to a valid string.

incorrectOptionExplanations.')' first and then '(' until both counts: A close can never come first.

promptVariants: Why prune at placement time instead of filtering at the end?
What invariant do the counts maintain?
cards.answer: Checking the constraints before adding a character keeps every partial string a valid prefix, so only valid strings are ever completed. Invariant: 0 <= closes <= opens <= n. Your version generates the invalid child and then rejects it at the top of the next call, which is correct but does extra calls.
cards.explanation: The number of results is the n-th Catalan number.

promptVariants: The number of results is the Catalan number, so the time is about ___ (excluding string building).
Complete the statement: The number of results is the Catalan number, so the time is about ___ (excluding string building).
What is the auxiliary space excluding the output?
Besides the output, how much memory does the parentheses generator use?
cards.answer: O(n): recursion depth up to 2n and the path list of up to 2n characters.

promptVariants: Why does your base case not `return` after appending, and what do the first-line checks do?
How would you restructure to prune earlier?
cards.answer: At length 2n it appends but keeps looping; the next calls are immediately rejected by the first-line checks (counts exceed n), so the result is right but wasteful - add a `return` after appending. The first line rejects invalid prefixes after the fact; better to test before recursing: `if opens < n: ...'('...` and `if closes < opens: ...')'...`.
keyPoints: Add return at the base case
